name: CIDR Calculator
description: Compute network address, mask, usable hosts and subnets, or convert an address range back into CIDR blocks.

hints.split: The split prefix must not be shorter than the original one; at most 256 subnets per call.
hints.hostCount: For IPv4 a `/31` counts 2 usable hosts and a `/32` counts 1; IPv6 has no unusable addresses.
hints.bits: Filled squares are the network bits (the first {prefix} of {bits} bits); hollow squares are host bits.

faq.a: IPv6 address counts can exceed 2⁶⁴, so only a decimal string keeps them exact.

faq.q: Why does a range produce several CIDRs?
faq.a: An arbitrary range usually cannot be a single CIDR, so the tool returns the minimal set.

faq.q: Does IPv6 have a broadcast address?
faq.a: No. The `broadcast` field is empty for IPv6.
